description: Hewlett Packard Enterprise focuses on enterprise IT solutions for customers across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific region. The company delivers products and services related to cloud computing, servers, storage, networking, artificial intelligence, and more. HPE has developed several of the fastest supercomputers in the world. With origins tracing back to 1939, the company was spun off from PC manufacturer HP in 2015 and has since expanded through several acquisitions.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
In 2015, when HPE was created in the wake of Hewlett-Packard’s separation, it made ambitious DEI goals a key part of its agenda. In February, it earned the top spot in Just Capital’s annual ranking, which takes into account social factors such as paying a fair living wage, creating American jobs, providing benefits to ensure work-life balance, and minimizing pollution. HPE was also dubbed the 15th-best workplace for parents last year, owing in large part to its flexible remote-work policies as well as its paid gender-neutral parental leave, bereavement leave after a miscarriage, and reimbursement for fertility expenses.
 

HPE’s remote-work model, which it rolled out during the pandemic, reimagined offices as cultural and collaboration hubs, with workspaces reflecting HPE’s hybrid vision—equipped with more meeting spaces and hybrid tech. Approximately 78% of team members say they are pleased with the model. And nearly 87% say they are happy with the connectivity tools that bring team members together. Among hybrid staff, 84% say their work environment enables them to perform their roles more effectively.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
IT firm Hewlett Packard emphasizes the importance of transparency between employees and management.

  • So far more than 3,500 employees have taken part in Mystery Coffee, a program where team members connect with others from around the globe for virtual one-on-one coffee breaks.

  • Employee wellness is a top priority at HPE, and team members worldwide can leave work three hours early on designated Wellness Fridays to spend time focused on their personal well-being.

  • Staff receive financial wellness help, too, with tools enabling them to assess their current money situation and receive insights on how to budget, manage debt, build savings, and protect their finances.

  • “HPE encourages employees to speak up, innovate, collaborate, be empowered, own our development, et cetera,” noted one employee.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Hewlett Packard Enterprise—which split from Hewlett-Packard in 2015 and focuses on information technology—saw order growth up 20% during the first fiscal quarter of 2022 as many U.S. companies continued to bring employees back to the office. Yet internally HPE has doubled down on the mental and emotional support offered to employees and focused on rolling out benefits like the Work That Fits Your Life program. As part of the initiative, rolled out in 2019, employees get access to three hours of paid time off one Friday a month and six full Fridays off each summer.

I honestly don't know what other company would allow me to do this. I am so grateful to HPE and always tell people how much I LOVE MY JOB AND COMPANY! My colleagues are not just my colleagues but my family! Now with being an Edge worker, it's only made my work life so much easier. Thank you HPE!!!”

rankings.title: Fortune Modern Board 25
rankings.itemDescription:
In 2014, the old-guard Silicon Valley giant Hewlett-Packard split into two companies, HP Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Since then, both have found strong footing in corporate governance: Both HPE and HP made this list. (HP is No. 9.)

That fact signals a remarkable turnaround. A little over a decade ago, Hewlett-Packard’s board endured multiple controversies involving proxy fights, unusual CEO transitions, and a scandal over surveillance of colleagues and journalists that led to the departure of four directors in 2011.

With those issues far in the past, HPE’s board earned the No. 2 spot on this list thanks to strengths in board expertise, gender equality, and board independence, among other criteria. The company specializes in enterprise information tech; it has recently seen particularly robust growth from its Intelligent Edge division, a data analytics and business intelligence platform.

HPE’s board is chaired by Patricia Russo, former CEO of Alcatel-Lucent, the communications company. Russo is also a director at Merck, General Motors, and the private equity firm KKR.

HPE’s directors’ careers reflect a wide range of expertise. Daniel Ammann is a former president of General Motors, as well as its former CFO, and until recently was CEO of GM Cruise LLC, a subsidiary of GM that focuses on autonomous vehicles. Pamela Carter is a former executive at Cummins, a machinery design and manufacturing company, where she was a business unit leader and general counsel; she chairs HPE’s HR and compensation committee. 

George R. Kurtz started his career at PwC and later founded a tech company that was acquired by McAfee. Mary Agnes Wilderotter chairs the audit committee and is the former CEO of Frontier Communications.

In the non-CEO realm, Raymond Ozzie is a former chief software architect at Microsoft and a fellow of the Computer History Museum; Gary M. Reiner is the former chief information officer at General Electric; and Raymond Lane is the former COO of Oracle and partner emeritus at the famed venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins.
